name: Romanian
script: Latin with extra letters: ă, â, î, ș, ț (comma below); left to right
basis: Durham University Romanian Beginners Steps 1–2 content summary, trimmed to A1
src: Durham University Centre for Foreign Language Study, 'Romanian language courses content summary' (PDF): topics and grammar for Beginners Step 1 (diacritics, first conjugation, a fi / a avea, pronouns, gender, articles, agreement) and Step 2 (accusative, dative, genitive, vocative, past tenses)
note: Stage 1 and 2 follow Durham Step 1, and stage 3 and 4 take the A1 parts of Step 2. Durham's Step 2 teaches four past tenses and the full genitive and dative; this roadmap keeps only perfectul compus and the fixed dative of îmi place, which is my judgment of A1 scope. The split into lessons, the să + verb and o să future lessons (from Durham's later steps) and all titles are common course practice and my own judgment.
hardest: The definite article stuck to the end of the noun: casa, studentul
Neuter nouns that are masculine in the singular and feminine in the plural
Irregular plurals (-i, -e, -uri) and sound changes in them
The vowels ă and â / î, which English does not have

items: Alphabet and sounds: ă, â / î, ș, ț
Spelling rules: ce / ci, ge / gi, che / chi, ghe / ghi
Greetings: bună ziua, salut, la revedere, mulțumesc
Polite 'you': tu, dumneavoastră, and domnul / doamna
a fi: sunt, ești, este… and Ce este asta?
Introducing yourself: Mă numesc…, Sunt din…
Three genders: un / o, and neuter nouns
The article on the end: un student / studentul, o casă / casa
Adjectives after the noun: un băiat bun, o fată bună
Question words: ce, cine, unde, când, cât
Present tense of -a verbs: a lucra, a cânta
a avea: have, and age (Am 25 de ani)
Present tense of -ea, -e, -i, -î verbs: a vedea, a merge, a dormi, a coborî
This and that: acesta / aceasta, acela / aceea
Family, jobs and possessives: fratele meu, sora mea
Numbers to 1000 and prices: Cât costă? lei, bani
Ordering food: Aș dori…, Vreau…, Nota, vă rog
Object pronouns: îl, o, îi, le; and pe for people
Time and days: Cât e ceasul? luni, marți
Directions: la dreapta, la stânga, drept înainte
să + verb: vreau să, pot să, trebuie să
Past: perfectul compus (am mâncat, am fost)
